text:
eli: FYI rolling alert from EU customers: sudden reconnect storm, clients reconnecting immediately after a 204 from edge. console shows repeated resume and duplicate billing spikes.
anya: 204 + Content-Type: text/event-stream? that's invalid for SSE clients. which edge?
eli: eu-edge canary v3. headers snippet in logs: `status=204, Content-Type: text/event-stream, X-Keepalive: true`.
shrey: ack. This came from our proxy normalization: when runtime sent an empty keepalive we switched body-less responses to 204 to save bandwidth. Problem: many SDKs treat 204 as terminal.
ops-bot: Canary eu-edge v3 at 1799987000 -> 15% traffic.
anya: mitigation idea: proxy should stop converting to 204; instead keep 200 and emit a comment line `:ka

` so SSE stays open. low-risk change.
eli: also billing change: protect by de-duping resume events server-side by (tenant,resume_id,last_event_id) within 15s to avoid double-charge while we roll out fix.
shrey: I'll prepare two PRs tonight: proxy change + billing dedupe TTL.
deploy-bot: Canary promoted to 45% at 1799987670.
anya: console work: surface a per-route metric `keepalive_status_mismatch` and add an alert at 0.5% in 1m window. link traces to route page.
eli: I'll notify affected customers and open a short incident. watching metrics.
shrey: quick repro instructions posted in PR description. planning hotfix if canary shows reduction in reconnects.
ops-bot: Alert suppressed after initial throttling, manual monitoring enabled.
eli: thanks all — prioritizing the proxy hotfix and billing guard.
